reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC3579-1-1.note: + TestRFC3579EAPAttributesServeALiveEAPMethod: the NAS that implements EAP-Message offers EAP (admin login, auth-method eap-mschapv2 completes, every Access-Request carries EAP-Message; red when authenticateEAP is disabled). - TestRFC3579SubscriberNASRefusesEAPMessage: the L2TP subscriber NAS, which offers PPP peers no EAP, answers CoA-Request and Disconnect-Request carrying EAP-Message with NAK Error-Cause 401, no event, no teardown; adding EAP-Message to coaSupportedAttrs/disconnectSupportedAttrs turns it red (recorded at coa.go unsupportedAttr). The older dictionary units stay as declaration-only supplementary tags.

RFC3579-1.2-1.note: negative compares verdict, profiles and source with and without a Notification carrying text; positive shows the message is delivered (logged, Notification Response sent) and not acted on

RFC3579-2.1-1.note: Access-Reject returns aaa.ErrAuthRejected with no profiles; the negative carries an EAP-Success inside the Access-Reject and still denies

RFC3579-2.1-3.note: positive compares User-Name to the Type-Data of the peer's EAP-Response/Identity read off the wire; negative checks every subsequent request (method Responses, not Identity) carries the same User-Name. Both clauses covered

RFC3579-2.2-1.note: only the Length field is validated under test (corruptEAPFrom declares a Length past the octets). Nothing forwards a server EAP packet with a wrong Code (not 1) or observes Identifier validation; the positive's Identifier-echo assertion is peer behaviour, not validation. Two of the three named fields unproven

RFC3579-2.6.3-1.note: Access-Reject carrying EAP-Success denies (TestRadiusAdminEapDecisionFollowsTheRadiusCode) and Access-Accept carrying EAP-Failure at the identity round grants (TestRadiusAdminEapAcceptWithEapFailureStillAuthorizes); both directions, fixture chosen so an early return on eapErr would go red

RFC3579-2.6.3-2.note: same pair as 2.6.3-1 read from the prohibition side: EAP content contradicting the code in either direction does not change the decision

RFC3579-2.6.4-1.note: a concluding Access-Accept's EAP Notification (and, in the negative, an undecodable EAP-Message) reaches the log before the code decides; a loop that reads resp.Code first and returns would log nothing

RFC3579-3-1.note: Row now quotes the MUST clause only (SHOULD half is RFC3579-3-2, {gap}). + TestRadiusAdminEapAccessRequestNamesTheNAS and TestRadiusAdminEapNamesTheNASWithoutASourceAddress: every Access-Request of the EAP conversation carries a non-empty NAS-Identifier, with and without a source address (one of the three suffices). - TestRadiusAdminEapWithNoNASIdentityIsNotSent: nasID empty and no IPv4 source -> Authenticate errors 'no NAS identity' and the server receives zero requests; observed red against the pre-fix exchange, which sent a zero-length NAS-Identifier. Producer exchange (authenticator.go) refuses before sending; NAS-IPv6-Address is never sent, so an IPv6-only source with no NAS-Identifier is refused, which is conservative, not non-conformant. Records at exchange observed red for all three units.

RFC3579-3-2.note: Applicable SHOULD not met. Every EAP-bearing Access-Request ze sends is the admin login's, built by (*radiusAuthenticator).exchange, which appends Service-Type, NAS-Identifier, User-Name and NAS-IP-Address and never NAS-Port or NAS-Port-Id: an admin login over SSH, the web or the API has no NAS port. The L2TP subscriber Access-Request sends NAS-Port (session id) but carries no EAP-Message. Row carries {gap}; not counted conformant.

RFC3579-3.1-1.note: split at 253 in order (join reproduces the packet), no foreign attribute inside the run (Message-Authenticator and State after it), and receive-side concatenation around foreign attributes

RFC3579-3.1-2.note: every sent Access-Request's EAP Length equals the whole run's octets, so a second packet riding along goes red; decoder refuses two separated runs in an Access-Challenge

RFC3579-3.1-3.note: every EAP-bearing Access-Request carries a 16-octet Message-Authenticator that the mock server verifies; encodeRequest refuses an EAP-Message without the placeholder and replaces it with the HMAC. Ze sends only Access-Requests, so the Challenge/Accept/Reject clauses bind the server

RFC3579-3.1-4.note: a forged challenge is discarded (retransmission observed, error is not a rejection); a verified challenge advances the conversation to a different second request

RFC3579-3.2-1.note: SignMessageAuthenticator matches an openssl HMAC-MD5 vector over the Access-Request, and a 0xff placeholder yields the same digest, so the field hashes as sixteen zero octets

RFC3579-3.3-1.note: encodeRequest refuses an Accounting-Request carrying EAP-Message or Message-Authenticator, and the control without either encodes

RFC3579-3.3-2.note: negative covers EAP-Message beside User-Password and beside CHAP-Password only. User-Password beside CHAP-Password is not tested, and ARAP-Password is in no pair: client.go oneCredentialType omits ARAP-Password (70) from its map, so an EAP-Message plus ARAP-Password Access-Request would encode

RFC3579-4.3.6-2.note: a successful and a rejected eap-mschapv2 login put an EAP-Message and no User-Password or CHAP-Password on every request, and the rejection produces no weaker retry
